archetypes.name: script-inventory
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims 'issue-input-file' subcommand already exists in stall-recovery-report.sh and produces the heading, but this is never verified against the script source; if that subcommand is absent or emits a different heading format, the entire fix premise is wrong.
archetypes.prompt_body: Locate `skills/implement/scripts/stall-recovery-report.sh` and verify the `issue-input-file` subcommand exists, synthesizes the `### [Bug] /implement stall: <class> at <step>` heading exactly as the plan claims, and honors `--implement-tmpdir`, `--classification-file`, and `--body-file` flags. Separately grep the full repository for every invocation of `stall-recovery-report.sh bug-body` and every invocation of `/larch:issue --input-file` that consumes stall-recovery output, to determine whether the plan's scope (only `stall-recovery.md` step 4) is complete or whether additional call sites would still route through the heading-less path after this change. Also confirm the `safe_class_value`/`safe_step_value` helpers used for title sanitization are defined and produce single-line, parser-safe output. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds test cases to two harnesses and references specific Makefile targets, but does not verify those targets are registered or that the parse-input.sh interface matches the assertion shape the plan prescribes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Open the `Makefile` (or wherever targets are defined) and confirm `test-stall-recovery-report` and `test-implement-structure` are registered targets that invoke the correct scripts. Read `skills/issue/scripts/parse-input.sh` to verify it emits `ITEMS_TOTAL` in the output format the plan expects (a key-value file consumed with a `kv` helper), and that mode=generic is what triggers the `### <title>` requirement — the plan asserts the raw `bug-body` output yields `ITEMS_TOTAL=0`; confirm the parser actually returns 0 rather than an error exit for a heading-less body. Check whether `skills/implement/scripts/test-stall-recovery-report.md` has a documented rule requiring `.md` to be updated alongside `.sh` in the same PR (the 'sibling rule' the plan cites), and flag if no such rule exists. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
